findings.title: Dependencies section is stale against the guide that actually shipped
findings.description: Description: The "Dependencies" bullet claims two guide items are "[s]till pending, both written after cf specifies them in slice design: the retroactive-marker rule, and the naming-conventions entry for the docs map file." Both have shipped: the guide CHANGELOG v0.22.3 (2026-10-21) records "Retroactive-slice marker in `guide.ai-project.brownfield-adoption` (Retroactive Slices)," and v0.22.6 (2026-10-25) records "Docs map file convention: `050-docs-map.{project}.md` … documented in `file-naming-conventions`" — confirmed present in `project-documents/ai-project-guide/file-naming-conventions.md:518` and implemented by `packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts` (slice 267). The arch's `dateUpdated` is 20261025, the same day as v0.22.6, so this is not an old revision — the "addressed in this revision" claim is contradicted by its own dependency record. The same bullet also says "cf releases that select the brownfield profile require at least v0.22.2," while shipped code requires `MIN_GUIDE_VERSION = '0.22.6'` (`packages/core/src/guides/guideMinimum.ts:5`), and 268 removes profile selection entirely, so the sentence is doubly obsolete. Relatedly, Responsibility Split row (c) still says "CF writes the architecture doc on **both paths**" although the amendment deleted the CF-only path, leaving one path.

findings.title: Slice 271's prompt-delivery contract doesn't specify the "Adoption Facts" section, and the live prompt hard-stops without it
findings.description: Description: The amendment says "the prompt's raw-probe branching goes away" and 268 deletes "the Adoption Facts section in `ContextTemplateEngine`" while 271 deletes "the probe JSON in the facts" — but nowhere in the amended text does it say what, if anything, the 271(b) primitive appends to the prompt it delivers. The exact artifact 271 fetches by key today — the Brownfield Adoption prompt in `prompt.ai-project.system.md` (guide v0.22.7) — instructs: "If the section is missing, stop and say: 'The Adoption Facts section is missing; cf build should always supply it…' Do not continue on any path," and its "Choose the path" block branches on `probe_version` and `surfaces.<s>.analysis_skill_installed` — fields 271 removes from cf. Until the external guide rewrite (272's dependency) lands, any consumer of the 271 primitive (squadron's `sq onboard`, which 272 is told to hand the contract) fetches a prompt that halts on every run. The "Guide release coupling" bullet only half-migrates the fail-fast rule: the parenthetical says it "moves to the prompt-delivery primitive," but the sentence immediately following still reads "If cf selects the brownfield profile and the installed guide lacks it, `cf build` fails with a named error" — the amended document names `cf build` as the failing component for behavior `cf build` no longer has. 272's success criteria ("no doc or guide prompt tells anyone to run `cf build` for adoption") also never names the missing-facts stop, so the alignment can pass while the stop survives. The 271 design must state: what the primitive appends, and its named error when the installed guide predates the 272 rewrite.

findings.title: After 268, the surviving greenfield entry path contradicts `cf next` on brownfield repos
findings.description: Description: The rework gives `cf next` one line for an unadopted brownfield repo: adoption arrives with `sq onboard`. But the only other live surface for such a repo, `cf build --phase concept`, delivers a concept conversation whose guide routing points brownfield users straight into the adoption machinery: `guide.ai-project.000-concept.md:24` ("If the project is an existing codebase with no planning artifacts, the concept is recovered from what exists rather than invented: follow `guide.ai-project.brownfield-adoption`") and `guide.ai-project.process.md:55` ("use `guide.ai-project.brownfield-adoption` instead of starting from a blank concept"). The adoption guide further declares the prompt "drives the work and owns the step-by-step procedure, including whether to use squadron's graph-based analysis or to work from the repo alone" — i.e., a self-serve adoption recipe, which ends at the hard stop described in the previous finding because the Adoption Facts no longer exist. So the same product tells a brownfield user both "adoption is parked until `sq onboard`" and "follow the adoption guide now." The Envisioned-State claim that the consolidated onboarding recipe "has no brownfield path" is only true at the recipe level; the concept conversation it hands off to still contains the brownfield branch in guide text. Slice 272's scope is "its brownfield prompt and adoption guide drop every `cf build` step and the raw-probe branching" — the `000-concept`, process-guide, and adoption-guide "How It Is Run" references are not named, so the alignment can complete while these contradictory pointers remain.

findings.title: A half-finished adoption is classified "already planned" and can never be completed
findings.description: Description: Detection order 2 says "Already planned: the repo holds a CF/SQ planning artifact (an initiative plan, an architecture doc or a slice plan). A concept on its own does not count," and the adoption flow (step 5) writes concept, then architecture, then the existing-state slice plan in one session. An adoption interrupted after the architecture write — crash, cost cap, PM walks away — leaves concept + derived architecture, no plan. Re-running `sq onboard` then hits step 2: "If the project is greenfield or already planned, adoption doesn't apply." The existing-state slice plan — the retroactive baseline — can never be written through the flow, and the principle that the marker is "set only by the adoption flow" leaves the user with no defined mechanism to finish. The old resume behavior ("a re-run resumes from whatever artifacts exist") lives only in the original profile contract, which the document explicitly preserves "for history" — i.e., it was deleted. The same hole swallows the shipped 0.19.x population: 261's shipped success criterion was "Adoption state persists and resumes across sessions," and users who held `adoption.state: in_progress` lose that resume path at 268/269 with adoption "parked" until an external repo ships `sq onboard`. The document names neither the partial-state case nor that user population.

findings.title: The derived architecture's preSlicePlan review gate is unexamined, and 240's record lacks the amendment 260 claims to make
findings.description: Description: The "Retroactive marker" bullet carefully engineers around the review gate for slice entries ("the code-review gate skips it rather than passing it… This amends the 240 gate rule"), and the code confirms it (`evaluateEntryGate` in `packages/core/src/introspection/reviewGate.ts`, `retroactiveRules.ts`). But the same interaction exists one level up and is never mentioned: the derived architecture is an ordinary `nnn-arch.*.md`, and when `workflow.review_enabled = true`, `ConsistencyChecker.ruleArchReviewGate` evaluates the `preSlicePlan` boundary for every discovered architecture file. A just-adopted project's derived architecture has no `NNN-review.arch.*.md`, `review: none` is explicitly not applicable to `preSlicePlan` (`evaluateExemption`), and nothing in the exemption logic recognizes `provenance: derived`. So an adopted project with gating on immediately carries a standing pending-review finding on the reverse-engineered doc — exactly the class of false trip the document designed against for slice entries ("would trip it on every entry"), with the difference that the architecture side has no stated decision. The document must say whether a derived architecture owes an arch review or is exempt, and how. Compounding this: "Dependencies" lists "Initiative 240 (complete): the review gate, **amended for retroactive entries**," but `240-arch.review-aware-workflow-gating.md` contains no trace of that amendment (its "Implementation reconciliation" block records the 911/912/919/924 changes, not the 263 entry-skip), so the canonical record of the gate does not reflect the rule 260 says it changed.

findings.title: Related-Work link to the arch review document is broken
findings.description: Description: The link `../reviews/260-review.arch.brownfield-adoption.md` does not resolve: `project-documents/user/` has no `reviews/` directory, and no file named `260-review.arch.brownfield-adoption.md` exists anywhere in the repository (verified by grep). The claim "(CONCERNS, 11 findings). All findings are addressed in this revision" therefore points at an artifact the repository cannot verify, and the slice plan's matching note ("the 260 arch review … is addressed … No re-review has been run") has the same unverifiable referent.

findings.title: Opt-out ordering mislabels already-planned repos as "greenfield"
findings.description: Description: The detection order checks "1. **Opted out:** the user said to treat the project as new. It is greenfield." before "2. **Already planned**." A repo that both opts out and holds planning artifacts (arch or slice plan present) therefore reports "greenfield" from the 271 state primitive and the `cf init` one-line — a false label for a repo full of planning artifacts, surfaced to `sq onboard` and `cf init` as an outcome rather than a suppressed brownfield classification. The shipped pre-rework code has the same ordering (`adoptionResolver.ts` returns the state-derived outcome before `findPlanningArtifacts` runs), so the document describes behavior faithfully; the gap is that the document never states the intended semantics — if opt-out is meant to suppress only the brownfield outcome, the report's outcome vocabulary should say so, since 271(a) makes this JSON a cross-repo contract.
